claims.claim: For every fixed 0<=p<1/2 the explicit finite no-query procedure has expected true cost at most C_p max(1,ln n) MST(d), for all n>=2 and all metrics and post-mask adversaries.
claims.evidence_location: accepted frozen original and full proof; manuscript Theorem 1.1
claims.finding: Same all-n, all-metric, all-post-mask-adversary scope, with explicit finite no-query procedure. No efficiency claim added.

claims.claim: Anand et al. prove O_p(log n) under arbitrary replacements for p<1/4.
claims.evidence_location: Anand et al. v1, Theorems 1.4/5.3
claims.finding: The arbitrary-increase/decrease upper bound has p<1/4 and expected O_p(log n) true cost.

claims.claim: Anand et al. prove a linear obstruction for p>=1/2.
claims.evidence_location: Anand et al. v1, Theorem 1.5 and Section 7
claims.finding: The source supplies a linear obstruction at or above one half. Positive-distance regularization is explicitly supplied and credited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Bateni et al. study the strong/weak distance-oracle model.
claims.evidence_location: Bateni et al., official PMLR paper pp.2-3
claims.finding: The weak/strong model and query types are described there.

claims.claim: Bateni et al. Theorem 4 gives no-strong-query O(sqrt(log n)) MST approximation assuming metric weak observations.
claims.evidence_location: Bateni et al., official PDF p.5, Theorem 4
claims.finding: The metric-weak-observation hypothesis and absence of strong queries are explicit; the expected approximation is O(sqrt(log n)).

claims.claim: Bateni et al. Appendix F.2.2 Theorem 32 gives a logarithmic obstruction for arbitrary corruptions at p=1/3.
claims.evidence_location: Bateni et al., official PDF p.46, F.2.2, Theorem 32
claims.finding: The stated corruption probability is 1/3 and the obstruction is logarithmic in expectation. No stronger parameter range is asserted.

claims.claim: Anand et al. Theorems 1.4/5.3 are the closest checked arbitrary-corruption upper bound; the present result closes their quarter-to-half gap, relative to cited versions.
claims.evidence_location: Anand et al. v1, Theorems 1.4/5.3; current arXiv record; bounded searches
claims.finding: The checked record still lists only v1. Comparison is bounded to cited versions; the paper disclaims exhaustive priority.

claims.claim: At p=1/3 the present upper bound has the order of the cited logarithmic obstruction.
claims.evidence_location: C01 and Bateni et al. Theorem 32
claims.finding: Logarithmic upper/lower order agrees at 1/3 only; the paper explicitly avoids extrapolating that lower bound to every p.

claims.claim: Repair benchmark, certificate minimization and preorder output build on Anand et al. Lemma 3.2 and Section 5.
claims.evidence_location: Anand et al. v1, Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.2, Definition 5.2 and Section 5 algorithm
claims.finding: Repair, minimum-certificate selection and first-appearance path are credited. The changed all-n expectation is proved in full.

claims.claim: The common-good-neighbor argument of Anand et al. Lemma 5.6 needs a good-pair fraction exceeding one half.
claims.evidence_location: Anand et al. v1, Lemma 5.6 proof, common-neighbor charging and final bad-density comparison
claims.finding: Their contradiction uses bad fraction 2p+2epsilon<1/2. Describing its good fraction as exceeding one half is accurate; it is a limitation of that argument, not an impossibility claim.

claims.claim: Positive density in every large disjoint rectangle plus order domination implies sum D_i <= (320r/eta)W+(8r/eta)M.
claims.evidence_location: frozen proof Section 1; accepted math report Section 1; manuscript Lemma 2.1
claims.finding: Constants 320 and 8, weighted order, positive hereditary rectangle density, every metric and vacuous cases match acceptance.

claims.claim: Hereditary rectangle density gives a star with r leaves in any 2 ceil(2r/eta) vertex set.
claims.evidence_location: same frozen transfer proof, hereditary-density paragraph
claims.finding: m>=2r averaging and the 2ceil(2r/eta) star condition are transcribed faithfully.

claims.claim: Cheap path edges sum to at most 64W; each expensive-edge interval has length D_i/32 with both endpoints within D_i/32 of each point it covers.
claims.evidence_location: same frozen transfer proof, interval definition
claims.finding: The 64 and 32 factors, strict inequalities, zeros and interval endpoints match.

claims.claim: A matching of short and long overlapping edges creates an empty r-by-r rectangle, so overlap is at most 8r/eta.
claims.evidence_location: same frozen transfer proof, overlap argument
claims.finding: Parity gives a matching; the top endpoint has no leaf neighbor anywhere, and the empty rectangle contradicts eta>0. No hidden algorithmic graph labels appear.

claims.claim: Integrating overlap controls all scales with D_max<=M, including the vacuous 2r>n case.
claims.evidence_location: same frozen transfer proof, integration
claims.finding: A single integral and diameter<=M give the accepted bound; the manuscript includes the vacuous case.

claims.claim: The credited repair has failure <=(n-1) beta^(n-2) and unconditional E[X]<=2(1+4/alpha)M, alpha=(1-p)^2.
claims.evidence_location: frozen proof Section 2; accepted math report Section 2; Anand Lemma 3.2 mechanism
claims.finding: The explicit unconditional all-n formula is proved in the manuscript and is not misrepresented as the exact original lemma statement.

claims.claim: Fixed-p rational parameters and finite tree/rectangle enumeration give an observable deterministic algorithm, even with zeros or vacuous rectangles.
claims.evidence_location: frozen proof observable-procedure section; accepted math report Section 3
claims.finding: Rational hardcoding, lexicographic choices and finite fallback are explicit and within the exact-arithmetic scope.

claims.claim: The uniform mask event has failure at most n^-12, uniformly over subsequent adversarial values and selected tree.
claims.evidence_location: frozen proof concentration section; accepted math report Section 2
claims.finding: The constants and n^-12 union bound are unchanged; uniformity is over masks before arbitrary replacement choices.

claims.claim: On E intersect F the repair tree qualifies and minimum observed cost is at most X; analysis graph density is at least eta.
claims.evidence_location: frozen proof composition; accepted math report Section 3
claims.finding: Qualification, comparison cost and positive density eta reproduce acceptance, with hidden graph used only for analysis.

claims.claim: The selected preorder has W<=2X and H-edge domination, yielding Y<=(320r/eta)(2X+M).
claims.evidence_location: same frozen composition; manuscript Section 5
claims.finding: Observed Euler nonnegative weights and W<=2X are preserved.

claims.claim: The good-event expectation is at most (320r/eta)(2B_p+1)M.
claims.evidence_location: same frozen composition; accepted math report Section 3
claims.finding: Unconditional nonnegative X expectation is used; no false independence or conditioning is introduced.

claims.claim: Every output has true cost <=(n-1)M, giving complementary expectation <=(1+2/alpha^3)M.
claims.evidence_location: same frozen expectation calculation
claims.finding: Universal output cost and series 2/alpha^3 match exactly, including beta=0 convention.

claims.claim: The explicit C_p is finite for fixed p<1/2, independent of aspect ratio and replacement magnitudes; averaging covers randomized adversaries.
claims.evidence_location: same frozen final theorem proof
claims.finding: Displayed C_p has the accepted finite fixed-p parameters and full adversary quantifiers.

claims.claim: The standard positive-distance two-cluster regularization preserves Anand et al. half-boundary obstruction, with expected crossing count 2ab/n and optimum 1+(n-2)delta.
claims.evidence_location: Anand et al. v1, Section 7 general model; accepted math report Section 5
claims.finding: The source construction has zero within-cluster distances; the manuscript transparently supplies the standard strictly positive delta version rather than attributing those formulas verbatim to the source.

claims.claim: Taking delta=n^-2 yields Omega(n) obstruction.
claims.evidence_location: accepted math report Section 5; manuscript displayed regularization
claims.finding: Substitution delta=n^-2 gives the credited Omega(n) boundary; no new lower bound is claimed.

claims.claim: Exact checks covered 160 integer metrics at n=8,12,16,24 including nonuniform weights and zeros.
claims.evidence_location: frozen interval-packing-check/validation records; accepted referee-verification record
claims.finding: 160 instances, the four sizes and listed metric families/weights match the saved records. These are finite checks, not metric-space coverage.

claims.claim: Exact checks covered 2,802,752 disjoint rectangles.
claims.evidence_location: frozen interval-packing-validation.json; audit/referee-verification.json
claims.finding: Both records give exactly 2,802,752 checked rectangles.

claims.claim: Exhaustive checks covered 33,866 pair masks for n=2,...,6 and p in {0,1/3,2/5,49/100}.
claims.evidence_location: same frozen validation and actual referee-verification repair results
claims.finding: The exact mask count is 33,866 across n=2,...,6, at the four listed rational probabilities. The description does not claim all real probabilities were enumerated.

claims.claim: A separate model context reconstructed the proof and recomputed finite checks using a different implementation.
claims.evidence_location: accepted referee math report and referee-verification code; check-math provenance
claims.finding: The distinct research/referee contexts and distinct verifier are documented; the manuscript calls this internal model checking, not external peer review or formal certification.

claims.claim: No polynomial/quasi-polynomial runtime or further application is established; constants deteriorate near one half.
claims.evidence_location: explicit manuscript procedure and accepted proof scope
claims.finding: Exhaustive search supports only finite computability; no efficient implementation or extra application is asserted. The displayed constants depend inversely on the below-half gap.
